cases.summary: Planned replacement of the peer runtime: after the peer and the local runtime each run a program named parent, fixture.peer restart stops the peer process and starts a fresh one, which proves the same machine id over a fresh challenge and takes the same actor (line epoch 2, no orphan notice left to replay). The peer's parent incarnation is lost on the new runtime (incarnation 0, not live), the local parent is preserved (incarnation 1, live, no kills), and a new terminal.run on the peer starts incarnation 1 there.

cases.summary: A machine named disconnected mirrored events through remote sequence 41 and lost its line: the injected input.send to disconnected/t1 is machine_unreachable with last_seen_seq "41" and the machine as target, and ghost/t1 is not_found; nothing runs locally. The peer is added and SIGSTOPped, an input.send to peer/parent is written to its line and the peer process is killed while the call is in flight: the call settles outcome_unknown with its op_id, the roster keeps the peer and the lost machine as unreachable, a later call to peer/parent is machine_unreachable (no local fallback) and the local parent is untouched. A plugin whose program prints boom and exits 3 is a durable failed run (exit_code 3, output kept, op receipt committed), while a sibling plugin with a missing program is listed executable_missing and refused action_unavailable.
